questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 25 play cricket, 20 play football, 15 play tennis. 8 play both cricket and football, 5 play both football and tennis, 6 play both cricket and tennis, 3 play all three. How many play at least one of the three sports?
Using the same data as above, how many students play EXACTLY two of the three sports?
A set A has 7 elements. How many subsets of A have an odd number of elements?
How many subsets of a 6-element set A contain a specific fixed element x ∈ A?
questions.solutionApproach: x is forced 'in'; the other 5 elements are free (in/out independently) → 2^5 = 32.

questions.question: Is the statement (A − B) ∪ (B − A) = (A ∪ B) − (A ∩ B) always TRUE for any two sets A, B?
questions.solutionApproach: Both sides equal the symmetric difference A △ B by definition — TRUE. Verify with A={1,2,3}, B={2,3,4}: LHS = {1}∪{4} = {1,4}; RHS = {1,2,3,4}−{2,3} = {1,4}. Matches.
questions.answer: TRUE — this is exactly the definition of symmetric difference.

questions.question: Let A be a 4-element set. What is the maximum number of subsets of A you can choose such that no chosen subset is a subset of another chosen subset?
questions.solutionApproach: This is Sperner's theorem: max antichain size = C(n, floor(n/2)) = C(4,2) = 6.
